Zwei Einheitsquadrate heißen benachbart, wenn sie eine gemeinsame Kante haben, und ein Pfad ist eine Folge von benachbarten Einheitsquadraten. Jedes Quadrat kann entweder weiß oder schwarz gefärbt sein. Bezeichne $N$ die Anzahl der Färbungen, bei denen es wenigstens einen schwarzen Pfad von der linken zur rechten Seite des Rechtecks gibt. Bezeichne $M$ die Anzahl der Färbungen, bei denen es wenigstens zwei disjunkte schwarze Pfade von der linken zur rechten Seite gibt. Zeige, dass $N^2 \geq M \cdot 2^{mn}$.
Finde alle Tupel positiver ganzer Zahlen $(m, n, p, q)$, sodass die Gleichung $p^{m} q^{n} = (p+q)^{2} + 1$ erfüllt ist.

Sei $ABCD$ ein gleichschenkliges Trapez mit $AB \parallel CD$ und $BC = AD$. Die Parallele zu $AD$ durch $B$ schneide die Senkrechte auf $AD$ durch $D$ im Punkt $X$. Die Parallele zu $BD$ durch $A$ schneide die Senkrechte auf $BD$ durch $D$ im Punkt $Y$. Zeigen Sie, dass die Punkte $C$, $X$, $D$ und $Y$ konzyklisch sind.

Sei ein Quadrat in $n > 1$ Rechtecke unterteilt, wobei die Seiten aller Rechtecke parallel zu den Seiten des Quadrats liegen. Jede Gerade, die parallel zu einer Seite des Quadrats verläuft und das Innere des Quadrats schneidet, muss dabei das Innere mindestens eines der Rechtecke durchqueren. Zeigen Sie, dass es in dieser Zerlegung immer mindestens ein Rechteck gibt, das keinen Punkt gemeinsam mit dem Rand des Quadrats hat.
Sei $p > 7$ eine Primzahl mit $p \equiv 1 \pmod{6}$, und sei $m = 2^p - 1$. Zeige, dass $2^{m-1} - 1$ durch $127m$ teilbar ist.

Sei $ABCD$ eine Raute mit einem spitzen Winkel im Punkt $A$. Auf den Diagonalen $AC$ und $BC$ liegen Punkte $M$ und $N$ derart, dass $|DM| = |MN|$. Bezeichne $P$ den Schnittpunkt von $AC$ und $DN$ und $R$ den Schnittpunkt von $AB$ und $DM$. Zeige, dass $|RP| = |PD|$.

Zwei sich in zwei verschiedenen Punkten $A$ und $B$ schneidende Kreise $\Gamma$ und $\Gamma'$ seien gegeben. Eine Gerade durch $B$ schneide $\Gamma$ in $C$ und $\Gamma'$ in $D$, wobei $B$ zwischen $C$ und $D$ liegt. Eine weitere Gerade durch $B$ schneide $\Gamma$ in $E$ und $\Gamma'$ in $F$, wobei $E$ zwischen $B$ und $F$ liegt. Es sei weiterhin $|CD| = |EF|$. Das Innere der Strecke $CF$ schneide $\Gamma$ in $P$ und $\Gamma'$ in $Q$. Seien $M$ und $N$ die Mittelpunkte der $C$ bzw. $F$ nicht enthaltenden Bögen $PB$ bzw. $BQ$ von $\Gamma$ und $\Gamma'$. Man beweise, dass das Viereck $CNMF$ ein Sehnenviereck ist.

Sei $\mathbb{Q}^+$ die Menge der positiven rationalen Zahlen. Eine Funktion $f: \mathbb{Q}^+ \to \mathbb{Q}^+$ heißt elastisch, wenn für alle $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}^+$ gilt:
$$
 f(x) + f(y) \geq 4f(x + y).
$$
a. Zeigen Sie, dass für jede elastische Funktion $f$ und alle positiven rationalen Zahlen $x, y, z$ gilt:
$$
 f(x) + f(y) + f(z) \geq 8f(x + y + z).
$$
b. Gibt es eine elastische Funktion $f$ und positiv rationale Zahlen $x, y, z$, so dass
$$
 f(x) + f(y) + f(z) < 9f(x + y + z)
$$
gilt?

Sei $n \geq 3$ eine nat\"urliche Zahl. Die Ecken eines regul\"aren $n$-Ecks seien im Uhrzeigersinn durch $1, 2, \ldots, n$ bezeichnet, wobei die Kante $i$ zwischen den Ecken $i$ und $i+1$ liegt, wobei $n+1 = 1$ gelten soll. Jeder Ecke $i$ wird eine nichtnegative ganze Zahl $e_i$ und jeder Kante $i$ eine nichtnegative ganze Zahl $k_i$ zugeordnet, sodass gilt:
(1) Das Tupel $(e_1, e_2, \ldots, e_n)$ ist eine Permutation von $(k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_n)$.
(2) F\"ur alle $1 \leq i \leq n$ gilt $k_i = |e_{i+1} - e_i|$, wobei $e_{n+1} = e_1$.

a) Zeigen Sie, dass f\"ur jedes $n \geq 3$ ein solches Tupel $(e_1, \ldots, e_n)$ existiert, das nicht identisch mit $(0, \ldots, 0)$ ist.

b) F\"ur jede positive nat\"urliche Zahl $m$ bestimmen Sie die kleinste Zahl $n$, so dass in den Tupeln $(e_1, \ldots, e_n)$ und $(k_1, \ldots, k_n)$ jeweils alle Zahlen von $0$ bis $m$ vorkommen.

Seien $d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_9$ neun verschiedene positive ganze Zahlen, und sei $P(n) = (n + d_1)(n + d_2) \cdots (n + d_9)$. Zeigen Sie, dass es eine ganze Zahl $N$ gibt, sodass für alle ganzen Zahlen $n \geq N$ die Zahl $P(n)$ durch eine Primzahl größer als 20 teilbar ist.

Sei $\Gamma$ der Umkreis des gleichschenkligen Dreiecks $ABC$ mit $AC = BC$. Auf der Seite $\overline{BC}$ sei ein Punkt $M$ gegeben. Auf dem Strahl $AM$ liege ein Punkt $N$ mit $|AN| = |AC|$, wobei $M$ zwischen $A$ und $N$ liegt. Der Umkreis des Dreiecks $CMN$ schneide $\Gamma$ in $C$ und einem weiteren Punkt $P$. Sei $Q$ der Schnittpunkt der Geraden $AB$ und $CP$. Man zeige, dass $\angle BMQ = \angle QMN$.

Seien $m, n \geq 4$ ganze Zahlen, und betrachte ein $m \times n$-Gitter, das von $m+1$ horizontalen und $n+1$ vertikalen Linien gebildet wird. Die Kreuzungspunkte dieser Linien heißen Knoten. Sei $P$ ein geschlossener, nicht-selbstüberschneidender Weg, der durch alle $(m-1)(n-1)$ inneren Knoten verläuft, aber keine der äußeren Knoten. Sei $A$ die Anzahl der inneren Knoten, durch die $P$ geradlinig hindurchgeht, $B$ die Anzahl der Gitterquadrate, bei denen $P$ genau zwei sich gegenüberliegende Kanten nutzt, und $C$ die Anzahl der Gitterquadrate, bei denen $P$ keine Kante nutzt. Zeige, dass $A = B - C + m + n - 1$.

Seien $k_1$ und $k_2$ zwei konzentrische Kreise in der Ebene mit Radien $r_1 = 13$ und $r_2 = 8$. Sei $AB$ ein Durchmesser von $k_1$ und $BC$ eine Sehne von $k_1$, die den Kreis $k_2$ im Punkt $D$ berührt. Berechne die Länge der Strecke $AD$.

Sei $n$ eine positive ganze Zahl. Betrachte disjunkte Paare $(a, b)$ mit $a, b \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, wobei $a \neq b$ und jedes Element der Menge $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ in höchstens einem Paar vorkommt. Bestimme die maximale Anzahl solcher Paare, sodass alle Paarsummen $a + b$ eindeutig sind und $a + b \leq n$ gilt.

Sei $a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \dots$ eine nicht abnehmende Folge positiver ganzer Zahlen. Eine positive ganze Zahl $n$ wird verlässlich genannt, wenn es ein positives ganzzahliges $i$ gibt mit $n = \frac{i}{a_i}$.\newline\newline Zeigen Sie: Wenn 2013 verlässlich ist, dann ist auch 20 verlässlich.

Eine positive ganze Zahl $n$ heißt neckisch, wenn es ganze Zahlen $a, b \geq 2$ gibt, sodass $n = a^b + b$. Untersuche, ob es 102 aufeinanderfolgende positive ganze Zahlen gibt, bei denen genau 100 neckisch sind.

Sei $ABC$ ein spitzwinkliges Dreieck mit $AB 
eq AC$. Bezeichne $D$ und $E$ die Mittelpunkte von $AB$ beziehungsweise $AC$. Die Umkreise von $BCD$ und $BCE$ schneiden den Umkreis von $ADE$ in weiteren Punkten $P$ beziehungsweise $Q$ (also $P 
eq D$ und $Q 
eq E$). Zeige, dass $AP = AQ$.

Bestimme alle positiven ganzen Zahlen $m$ mit der Eigenschaft, dass die rekursiv definierte Folge $a_0 = \frac{2m + 1}{2}$ und $a_{k+1} = a_k \cdot \lfloor a_k \rfloor$ für $k \geq 0$ mindestens einen ganzzahligen Term enthält.

Seien $k$ und $n$ positive ganze Zahlen mit $n > k$. Ein Binärwort der Länge $n$ ist eine Folge von $n$ Symbolen, wobei jedes Symbol entweder 0 oder 1 ist. Anja wählt ein Binärwort der Länge $n$ aus und schreibt anschließend alle Binärwörter an die Tafel, die sich von ihrem ausgewählten Wort in genau $k$ Positionen unterscheiden. Bernhard tritt ein, wird von Anja über den Wert von $k$ informiert, und betrachtet die Menge an Binärwörtern an der Tafel. Wie viele verschiedene Versuche benötigt Bernhard mindestens, um sicher das ursprünglich ausgewählte Binärwort zu identifizieren, in Abhängigkeit von $k$ und $n$?

Sei $d$ eine positive ganze Zahl und $\left(a_i\right)_{i=1}^{\infty}$ eine Folge positiver ganzer Zahlen, in der jede positive ganze Zahl genau einmal vorkommt. Es gelte außerdem $\left|a_{i+1} - a_i\right| \leq 2d$ für alle $i \geq 10^{100}$. Zeigen Sie, dass unendlich viele Indizes $j$ existieren mit $\left|a_j - j\right| < d$.

Bestimme alle ganzen Zahlen $n \geq 2$ mit folgender Eigenschaft: Für jede Folge $m_1, m_2, \ldots, m_n$ ganzer Zahlen (nicht notwendigerweise paarweise verschieden), bei der die Summe $m_1 + m_2 + \cdots + m_n$ nicht durch $n$ teilbar ist, gibt es einen Index $i$ mit $1 \leq i \leq n$, so dass keine der $n$ Summen $$ m_i,\ m_i + m_{i+1},\ m_i + m_{i+1} + m_{i+2},\ \ldots,\ m_i + m_{i+1} + \cdots + m_{i+n-1} $$ durch $n$ teilbar ist, wobei $m_{j} = m_{j - n}$ für $j > n$ gelte.

Sei $\mathbb{Q}^{+}$ die Menge der positiven rationalen Zahlen. Bestimme alle Funktionen $f: \mathbb{Q}^{+} \to \mathbb{Q}^{+}$, welche die Gleichung $$ f\left(x^2 f(y)^2\right) = f\left(x^2\right) f(y) $$ für alle $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}^{+}$ erfüllen.

Bestimmen Sie, ob es eine Menge $M$ von positiven ganzen Zahlen gibt, so dass für jede positive rationale Zahl $r < 1$ genau eine endliche Teilmenge $S \subseteq M$ existiert, für die $\sum_{s \in S} \frac{1}{s} = r$ gilt.

Sei $\varepsilon > 0$ eine reelle Zahl. Zeigen Sie, dass es ganze Zahlen $a, b, c$, nicht alle null, gibt mit $|a\sqrt{2} + b\sqrt{3} + c\sqrt{5}| < \varepsilon$. Zeigen Sie außerdem, dass für jedes solche Tripel $(a, b, c) \neq (0, 0, 0)$ mindestens einer der Werte $|a|$, $|b|$, oder $|c|$ größer als $\frac{\varepsilon^{-1/3}}{\sqrt{30}}$ ist.
Beweisen Sie, dass für jede nichtnegative ganze Zahl $z$ ein eindeutiges geordnetes Paar $(m, n)$ positiver ganzer Zahlen $m, n$ existiert, sodass $2z = (m + n)^2 - m - 3n$ gilt.

Sei $ABC$ ein gleichschenkliges Dreieck mit $\overline{BC} = \overline{CA}$. Es sei $D$ ein Punkt im Inneren der Seite $AB$ mit $\overline{AD} < \overline{DB}$. Auf den Seiten $BC$ und $CA$ seien Punkte $P$ und $Q$ so, dass $\angle DPB = \angle AQD = 90^\circ$. Die Mittelsenkrechte der Strecke $PQ$ schneide $CQ$ im Punkt $E$, und die Umkreise von $ABC$ und $QPC$ schneiden sich in einem Punkt $F \neq C$. Zeigen Sie: Wenn $P, E$ und $F$ kollinear sind, dann ist $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$.

Sei $m$ eine positive ganze Zahl, und sei $A \subseteq \{0,1,2, \ldots, 5^{m}\}$ eine Menge mit $|A| = 4m + 1$. Zeigen Sie, dass es drei Elemente $a, b, c \in A$ mit $a < b < c$ und $c + 2a > 3b$ gibt.

Sei $ABCD$ ein Parallelogramm mit $|AC| = |BC|$. Ein Punkt $P$ liegt auf dem Strahl $AB$ so, dass $B$ zwischen $A$ und $P$ ist. Der Umkreis von Dreieck $ACD$ schneidet die Strecke $PD$ in einem weiteren Punkt $Q$ außer $D$. Der Umkreis von Dreieck $APQ$ schneidet die Strecke $PC$ in einem weiteren Punkt $R$ außer $P$. Zeigen Sie, dass die drei Geraden $CD$, $AQ$ und $BR$ konkurrent sind.

Sei $k$ eine positive ganze Zahl, und betrachte die Menge $K = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \mid 0 \leq x, y < 2k\}$, also die Menge aller Gitterpunkte mit nichtnegativen ganzzahligen Koordinaten kleiner als $2k$. Sei $V$ eine Menge von $k^2$ nicht-ausgearteten Vierecken, wobei\ i) alle Ecken der Vierecke in $V$ Elemente von $K$ sind, und\ ii) jeder Punkt in $K$ genau ein Viereck in $V$ als Ecke teilt.\ Bestimme den maximal möglichen Wert der Gesamtfläche aller Vierecke in $V$.

Let triangle $ABC$ be given such that $AB < AC$. Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$, and let the angle bisector from $A$ intersect the circumcircle of triangle $BCI$ at a point $N \neq I$. 
(i) Express the angles of triangle $BCN$ in terms of the angles of triangle $ABC$,
(ii) identify the center of the circumcircle of triangle $BCI$.

Given triangle $AB\Gamma$ with angle $\hat{A} = 105^\circ$ and angle $\hat{\Gamma} = \frac{\hat{B}}{4}$:

α. Find the measures of angles $\hat{B}$ and $\hat{\Gamma}$.

β. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $AB\Gamma$, and let $\Delta$ be the point diametrically opposite to $B$. Prove that the perpendicular distance from $\Gamma$ to the line segment $B\Delta$ is equal to $\frac{B\Delta}{4}$.

Given a circular annulus bounded by two concentric circles of radii $R = 11r$ and $R - 2r$, place as many non-overlapping circles of radius $r$ as possible such that each is tangent to both boundaries of the annulus. Find the maximum number of such circles. (It is given that $9.94 < \sqrt{99} < 9.95$)
Determine all integers $ n $ such that the expression $ \frac{9n^2 + 31}{n^2 + 7} $ is an integer.

Find all positive integers $n$ such that there exist real numbers $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ in $[-4, 2]$ satisfying:
- $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i \ge n$,
- $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2 \le 4n$,
- and $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^4 \ge 34n$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with circumcenter $O$, and let $A_1, B_1, C_1$ be the midpoints of sides $BC, AC$, and $AB$, respectively. Define points $A_2, B_2, C_2$ such that $\overrightarrow{OA_2} = \lambda \cdot \overrightarrow{OA_1}$, $\overrightarrow{OB_2} = \lambda \cdot \overrightarrow{OB_1}$, and $\overrightarrow{OC_2} = \lambda \cdot \overrightarrow{OC_1}$, where $\lambda > 0$. Prove that the lines $AA_2$, $BB_2$, and $CC_2$ are concurrent.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a scalene triangle with $AB < AC$, and let $\omega$ be its circumcircle with center $O$ and radius $R$. The circle centered at $A$ with radius $AB$ intersects $BC$ at $E$ and $\omega$ at $F$. The line $EF$ intersects $\omega$ again at $D$ and intersects $AC$ at $M$. The line $AD$ intersects $BC$ at $K$, and the circumcircle of triangle $BKD$ intersects $AB$ at $L$. Prove that the points $K$, $L$, and $M$ are collinear and lie on a line parallel to $BF$.
Find all integer solutions $ (x, y) $ to the equation $ x^3 y^2 (2y - x) = x^2 y^4 - 36 $.
Let $A$ be a finite set of positive real numbers. Define $B = \left\{\frac{a}{b} : a, b \in A\right\}$ and $C = \left\{ab : a, b \in A\right\}$. Prove that $|A| \cdot |B| \le |C|^2$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle with $AB < AC$, inscribed in a circle $\omega$ with center $O$ and radius $R$. The altitude from $A$ to $BC$ is extended to meet $\omega$ again at $E$. Let $\mu$ be the perpendicular bisector of segment $AB$, and let $L$ be the intersection point of $\mu$ and $AD$. The line $BL$ intersects $AC$ at $M$ and $\omega$ again at $N$. The segment $EN$ intersects $\mu$ at $Z$. Prove that: $$ MZ \perp BC \Leftrightarrow (AC = BC \text{ or } Z = O). $$

Let $ x, y, z $ be positive real numbers such that $ x + y + z = 12 $. Prove that $ \frac{x}{y} + \frac{y}{z} + \frac{z}{x} + 3 \ge \sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y} + \sqrt{z} $, and determine the conditions under which equality holds.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB < AC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of segment $BC$. On side $AB$, choose a point $D$ such that the segment $CD$ intersects the median $AM$ at a point $E$ satisfying $AD = DE$. Prove that $AB = CE$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute, scalene triangle with $AB < AC$, and let $c(O, R)$ be its circumcircle. The circle centered at $B$ with radius $AB$ intersects side $AC$ at point $K$ and the circumcircle $c$ at point $E$. The line $KE$ intersects the circumcircle $c$ again at point $F$. The line $BO$ intersects $KE$ at point $L$ and $AC$ at point $M$. The line $AE$ intersects $BF$ at point $D$. Prove that the polygons $DLMF$ and $BDKME$ are cyclic.
Prove the inequality $\left(a+2b+\frac{2}{a+1}\right)\left(b+2a+\frac{2}{b+1}\right) \ge 16$ holds for all positive real numbers $a$ and $b$ satisfying $ab \ge 1$.

Let $A = \overline{abcd} = a \cdot 10^3 + b \cdot 10^2 + c \cdot 10 + d$ be a four-digit positive integer with digits satisfying $a \ge 7$ and $a > b > c > d > 0$. Let $B = \overline{dcba} = d \cdot 10^3 + c \cdot 10^2 + b \cdot 10 + a$. If the sum $A + B$ has all odd digits, find all possible values of $A$.

Let $V$ be a finite set of competitors in a competition, and define a friendship graph $G = (V, E)$, where an edge exists between two competitors if and only if they are friends. A cycle $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_n$ ($n \ge 3$) is called a weekly-friendly cycle if $A_i$ is not adjacent to $A_{i+1}$ for $1 \le i \le n$ (with $A_{n+1} = A_1$), and all other pairs of vertices in the cycle are adjacent. Suppose that for every competitor $C$ and every weekly-friendly cycle $\mathcal{A}$ not containing $C$, the set of vertices in $\mathcal{A}$ that are not adjacent to $C$ contains at most one element. Prove that the graph $G$ is 3-colorable, i.e., the competitors can be partitioned into three rooms such that no two competitors in the same room are non-friends.
Determine all positive integer solutions $(x, y, z)$ to the equation $\frac{1}{x} + \frac{2}{y} - \frac{4}{z} = 1$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with midpoint $M$ of side $BC$. Construct a parallelogram $BCDE$ outside of $\triangle ABC$ such that $BE \parallel AM$ and $BE = AM / 2$. Prove that the line $EM$ passes through the midpoint of segment $AD$.

Let $P(x) = a x^3 + (b - a) x^2 - (b + c) x + c$ and $Q(x) = x^4 + (b - 1) x^3 + (a - b) x^2 - (a + c) x + c$ be polynomials in $x$, where $a, b, c$ are nonzero real numbers with $b > 0$. Suppose that $P(x)$ has three distinct real roots $x_0, x_1, x_2$ that are also roots of $Q(x)$. Then:
(a) Prove that $abc > 28$.
(b) If $a, b, c$ are nonzero integers with $b > 0$, determine all possible values of $a, b, c$.
Find all pairs of nonnegative integers $(m, n)$, with $m \ge n$, such that $(m+n)^3$ divides $2n(3m^2 + n^2) + 8$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle with $AB \leq AC$, and let $\omega$ denote its circumcircle with center $O$ and radius $R$. Let $\ell$ be the tangent to $\omega$ at point $C$, and consider the line through $A$ that is perpendicular to $\ell$; let it intersect $\ell$ at a point $D$.

(a) If triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with $AB = AC$, prove that $CD = \frac{BC}{2}$.

(b) If $CD = \frac{BC}{2}$, prove that triangle $ABC$ is isosceles.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles acute-angled triangle with $AB = AC$. Let $CH$ be an altitude of the triangle. The circle $c_2(C, CH)$ intersects $AC$ at point $K$, the extension of $AC$ at point $Z$, and the circle $c_1(B, BH)$ at point $E$. Finally, $HZ$ intersects the circle $c_1$ at point $M$. Prove that

a. $\angle ZHE = 45^\circ$

b. The points $E$, $M$, and $K$ are collinear.

c. The line $BM$ is parallel to the line $EC$.

Let $ABCD$ ($AD\parallel BC$) be a right trapezium with $\angle A = \angle B = 90^\circ$ and $AD < BC$. Let $E$ be the intersection point of the non-parallel sides $AB$ and $CD$, let $Z$ be the reflection of $A$ across the line $BC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $EZ$. Suppose that the line $CM$ is perpendicular to the line $DZ$. Prove that the line $ZC$ is perpendicular to the line $CE$.

Let $ABCD$ be a square with side length $\alpha$. Points $E$ and $Z$ lie on side $AD$ such that $DE = \frac{\alpha}{3}$ and $AZ = \frac{\alpha}{4}$. If the lines $BZ$ and $CE$ intersect at point $H$, express the area of triangle $BCH$ in terms of $\alpha$.

Let triangle $ABC$, with $AB < AC$, be inscribed in a circle $c$ centered at $O$. Let $G$ denote the centroid of triangle $ABC$, and let $D, E, F$ be the feet of the altitudes from $A, B, C$, respectively. If the rays $AG$ and $GD$ intersect the circumcircle $c$ again at points $M$ and $N$, respectively, prove that the points $F, E, M, N$ lie on a common circle.
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Define $A = \frac{4n!}{n!\cdot 2n!}$. Prove that $A$ is an integer and that $2^{n+1}$ divides $A$.

Let triangle $ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle inscribed in a circle $c$ with center $O$ and radius $R$. Let $F$ be a point on segment $AB$ such that $AF < \frac{AB}{2}$. Consider the circle $c_1$ centered at $F$ with radius $FA$, which intersects the line $OA$ at a point $A'$ and the circle $c$ at a point $K$. Prove that the points $B$, $K$, $F$, $A'$, and $O$ lie on a common circle.
Determine all integer triples $(a, b, c)$ satisfying $a > 0 > b > c$ and $a + b + c = 0$, such that the expression $N = 2017 - a^3b - b^3c - c^3a$ yields a perfect square.
Show that for every positive integer $n$, the expression $7^{2n} - 48n - 1$ is divisible by $9$.

Let $ p \ge 2 $ be a prime number. Angelo and Vangelis alternate turns placing a digit in one of $ p $ adjacent empty boxes. Angelo moves first and the game ends when all boxes are filled, forming a $ p $-digit number $ M $ (possibly with leading zeros). Angelo's objective is to ensure that $ M $ is divisible by $ p $, while Vangelis tries to prevent this. Prove that Angelo has a winning strategy.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $AB > AC$. Let point $D$ be on the side $AB$ such that $BD = AC$. We draw the circle $\gamma$ passing through $D$ and tangent to the side $AC$ at $A$. The circumcircle $\omega$ of the triangle $ABC$ meets circle $\gamma$ at $A$ and $E$. Prove that $E$ is the point of intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of the segments $BC$ and $AD$.

Consider an equilateral triangle of side length $k$ cm, subdivided into $k^2$ small equilateral triangles of side length $1$ cm using parallel lines, forming a grid. Assign the integers $1$ through $k^2$ to the small triangles such that each integer appears exactly once. A regular hexagon of side length $1$ cm is formed with vertices from the grid. The value of a hexagon is defined as the sum of the integers assigned to its six small triangles. Determine, as a function of $k$, the maximum possible total value of all such hexagons.

Consider a sequence $a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_\nu, \ldots$, $\nu \in \mathbb{N}$, of non-negative integers, not necessarily distinct, satisfying the conditions:

(i) $0 \le a_i \le i$ for all integers $i \ge 0$,

(ii) $\binom{n}{a_0} + \binom{n}{a_1} + \cdots + \binom{n}{a_n} = 2^n$ for all integers $n \ge 0$.

Prove that for each non-negative integer $k$, there exists an index $i$ such that $a_i = k$.

In triangle $ABC$ with $AB < AC$, let the perpendicular bisector of $BC$ meet $AB$ and $AC$ at points $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Let $H$ denote the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$, and let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of $BC$ and $PQ$, respectively. Prove that the lines $HM$ and $AN$ intersect at a point lying on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.

Let $v$ be an integer greater than $1$. Consider a $v \times v$ grid where each cell contains an integer that is congruent to $1$ modulo $v$. Furthermore, assume that the sum of the elements in each row and in each column is congruent to $v$ modulo $v^2$. Let $\Gamma_i$ denote the product of the entries in the $i^\text{th}$ row, and $\Sigma_j$ the product of the entries in the $j^\text{th}$ column. Show that the total row product sum $\Gamma_1 + \Gamma_2 + \dots + \Gamma_v$ is congruent to the total column product sum $\Sigma_1 + \Sigma_2 + \dots + \Sigma_v$ modulo $v^4$.

Given an equilateral triangle with altitude $1$ and an interior point $P$, let $x$, $y$, and $z$ denote the perpendicular distances from $P$ to the three sides of the triangle. Prove the inequality: $$ x^2 + y^2 + z^2 \geq x^3 + y^3 + z^3 + 6xyz. $$

Let $ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle with $AB < AC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$, and let $BE$ and $CF$ be the altitudes from $B$ and $C$ respectively. The line $EF$ intersects $BC$ at point $G$.

a. Determine the angles of triangle $EFM$ in terms of the angle $\angle BAC$.

b. Determine the angle $\angle BGF$ in terms of the angles $\angle ABC$ and $\angle ACB$.

\textbf{Part 1:} Determine the real number $ k $ such that the cubic polynomial $ P(x) = x^3 - kx + 2 $ has $ x = 2 $ as a root. For this value of $ k $, express $ P(x) $ as a product of two polynomials with integer coefficients.

\textbf{Part 2:} Let $ a $ and $ b $ be positive real numbers satisfying $ 2a + b + \frac{4}{ab} = 10 $. Determine the maximum possible value of $ a $.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$, and let $P$ be a point inside the triangle such that $\angle PBC = 30^\circ$, $\angle PBA = 50^\circ$, and $\angle BPC = 55^\circ$.

a. Prove that $\angle ABC = \angle ACB = 80^\circ$.

b. Determine the measure of $\angle PAC$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with sides satisfying $AB < AC < BC$. On the ray $BC$, take a point $D$ such that $BD = BA$, and on the ray $CB$, take a point $E$ such that $CE = CA$. Let $K$ be the circumcenter of triangle $ADE$, and define points $F$ and $G$ as the intersections of lines $AD$ with $KC$ and $AE$ with $KB$, respectively. Prove that the circumcircle of triangle $KDE$, denoted $c_1$, the circle centered at $F$ with radius $FE$, denoted $c_2$, and the circle centered at $G$ with radius $GD$, denoted $c_3$, all pass through a common point lying on line $AK$.

Let $n > 4$ be a positive integer such that $4$ divides $n$. Let $A_n$ be the sum of all odd positive divisors of $n$, and let $B_n$ be the sum of all even positive divisors of $n$ excluding $n$ itself. Define $f(n) = B_n - 2A_n$. Determine the smallest possible value of $f(n)$ and find all positive integers $n$ for which this minimum is achieved.

Consider a $ 3n \times 3n $ chessboard where each square is colored black or white. The coloring is such that starting from the top-left corner, every third diagonal is black and the remaining squares are white. In each move, we select a $ 2 \times 2 $ square and apply the following transformation: white squares become orange, orange squares become black, and black squares become white. The goal is to transform the board such that all initially black squares become white and all initially white squares become black. Prove the following: a) This transformation is not possible when $ n = 3 $. b) This transformation is possible when $ n = 2 $.

Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function satisfying the inequality
$$f(x+y)f(x-y) \geq (f(x))^2 - (f(y))^2$$
for all real numbers $x$ and $y$. Suppose further that there exist real numbers $x_0$ and $y_0$ such that
$$f(x_0 + y_0)f(x_0 - y_0) > (f(x_0))^2 - (f(y_0))^2.$$
Prove that $f(x) \geq 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, or $f(x) \leq 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with circumcircle $\omega(O, R)$. A circle $\gamma$ passes through $O$ and $B$ and is tangent to the line $AB$ at $B$. Let a circle $\kappa$ intersect $\omega$ at a second point $P \neq B$. A circle passing through $P$ and $C$ and tangent to line $AC$ at $C$ intersects $\gamma$ at a point $M \neq P$. Prove that $MP = MC$.

Let triangle $ABC$ have incentre $I$. Let $M_A$, $M_B$, and $M_C$ be the midpoints of sides $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$, respectively, and let $H_A$, $H_B$, and $H_C$ be the feet of the altitudes from $A$, $B$, and $C$ to the opposite sides. Let $\ell_b$ be the tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ at $B$, and let $\ell'_b$ be the reflection of $\ell_b$ over the line $BI$. Define $P_B$ as the intersection of line $M_A M_C$ with $\ell_b$, and $Q_B$ as the intersection of line $H_A H_C$ with $\ell'_b$. Define $\ell_c, \ell'_c, P_C$, and $Q_C$ similarly. Let $R$ be the intersection point of lines $P_B Q_B$ and $P_C Q_C$. Prove that $RB = RC$.
Show that for all positive real numbers $ x, y, z $, the inequality $$ \frac{xyz(x + y + z + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2})}{(x^2 + y^2 + z^2)(xy + yz + zx)} \le \frac{3 + \sqrt{3}}{9} $$ holds.

Given a triangle $\triangle ABC$, let the internal angle bisectors of $\angle A$, $\angle B$, and $\angle C$ meet the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ again at points $P$, $Q$, and $R$, respectively. Prove that the sum $AP + BQ + CR$ is greater than the perimeter of triangle $ABC$, i.e., $AP + BQ + CR > AB + BC + CA$.
Show that the sum $ S = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{2k + 1} $ is not an integer for any integer $ n \ge 1 $.

Let $ ABC $ be a triangle. On the sides $ AB $, $ BC $, and $ CA $, construct isosceles triangles $ ABX $, $ BCY $, and $ CAZ $ outwardly such that $ XA = XB $, $ YB = YC $, and $ ZC = ZA $, and all three triangles are similar. Prove that the lines $ AY $, $ BZ $, and $ CX $ intersect at a common point.

Let $f$ be a function on the positive real numbers satisfying:
(1) $f(1) = 1$,
(2) $f(x + 1) = x f(x)$ for all $x > 0$,
and (3) $f(x) = 10^{g(x)}$ for a function $g$ on $\mathbb{R}$ that is concave, i.e., satisfying
$$
 g(ty + (1 - t)z) \leq t g(y) + (1 - t) g(z)
$$
for all $y, z \in \mathbb{R}$ and $t \in [0, 1]$.

a. Prove the inequality $t [g(n) - g(n - 1)] \leq g(n + t) - g(n) \leq t [g(n + 1) - g(n)]$ for all integers $n$ and $t \in [0, 1]$.

b. Prove that $\frac{4}{3} \leq f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \leq \frac{4}{3} \sqrt{2}$.

Let $G$ be a complete graph on $n$ vertices in the plane, with each edge painted one of $k$ available colours.

a. For $n = 6$ and $k = 3$, demonstrate that there exists an edge colouring of $G$ such that no monochromatic cycle exists.

b. Show that for any positive integer $k$, if $n \ge 2k + 1$, then every such colouring of $G$ must contain at least one monochromatic cycle.

Let $ABCD$ be a trapezoid such that $AB \parallel CD$, with $AB > CD$ and side $AD$ longer than side $BC$. Prove the following:
1. The angle $\angle CBA$ is greater than $\angle DAB$,
2. The diagonal $AC$ is longer than the diagonal $BD$.

There are $n$ ($n \ge 3$) subjects, each with a test paper taken by students. For each subject, exactly three students achieve the best score in that subject. Moreover, for any pair of subjects, there is exactly one student who achieves the best score in both. Find the minimal value of $n$ such that these conditions guarantee that there is a single student who achieves the best score in all $n$ subjects.

Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $\triangle ABC$ with side lengths satisfying $AB > AC > BC$. Let $D$ be a point on the minor arc $BC$ (not containing $A$) of the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$, such that $AD$ is not a diameter. Define points $E$ and $F$ on segment $AD$ such that $OE \perp AB$ and $OF \perp AC$. Let $P$ be the intersection point of lines $BE$ and $CF$. If the condition $PB = PC + PO$ holds, prove that $\angle BAC = 30^\circ$.
Determine all integers $ n \ge 3 $ for which there exists a regular $ n $-gon with all vertices at lattice points on the coordinate plane, where a lattice point is a point with integer coordinates.

Let $ ABC $ be a triangle such that $ BC > AC > AB $. A point $ D $ lies on side $ BC $, and a point $ E $ lies on the ray $ BA $ beyond $ A $ with $ BD = BE = AC $. Let $ P $ be a point on segment $ AC $ such that the points $ E, B, D, P $ lie on a circle, and let $ Q $ be the second intersection point of the line $ BP $ with the circumcircle of triangle $ ABC $. Prove that $ AQ + CQ = BP $.
Let $ a, b, c $ be positive real numbers. Prove that the inequality $ \frac{a}{b+c} + \frac{b}{c+a} + \frac{c}{a+b} \ge \frac{3}{2} $ holds.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. A point $D$ lies on the minor arc $AC$ of the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$. If $E$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to line $BD$, prove that $BE = ED + DC$.

Determine the largest real number $ K $ for which the inequality $$ (u^2 - 4vw)^2 > K(2v^2 - uw)(2w^2 - uv) $$ is valid for all positive real numbers $ u $, $ v $, and $ w $ satisfying $ u^2 > 4vw $. Provide a justification for your result.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $M$ the midpoint of $AC$, and let $D$ be a point on $AB$. Suppose that the lines $BM$ and $CD$ intersect at a point $O$ such that $AB = CO$. Let $E$ be a point on $AC$ such that $DE \parallel BM$. Prove that $AB \perp BC$ if and only if the quadrilateral $ADOM$ is cyclic.

Let $n \ge 2$ and consider a sequence of positive real numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{n+1}$ such that the differences $a_2 - a_1, a_3 - a_2, \dots, a_{n+1} - a_n$ are all non-negative and equal. Prove the inequality
$$
\sum_{k=2}^{n} \frac{1}{a_k^2} \le \frac{n-1}{2} \cdot \frac{a_1 a_n + a_2 a_{n+1}}{a_1 a_2 a_n a_{n+1}}.
$$
Also determine the conditions under which equality occurs.

A positive integer $ n $ is called *good* if there exist positive integers $ a $ and $ b $ such that $ a + b = n $ and $ ab $ is divisible by $ n $. If $ a $ and $ b $ can also be distinct, then $ n $ is said to be *very good*. For example, $ 9 $ is good since $ 3 + 6 = 9 $ and $ 3 \times 6 $ is divisible by $ 9 $, and it is very good because $ 3 $ and $ 6 $ are distinct.

a. Given that $ 2003 $ is prime, prove that $ 2003 $ is not good.

b. Determine whether $ 2002 $ is good.

c. Find all positive integers that are good but not very good, and justify your answer.

Define $ f(n) $ to be the count of $ 2n $-digit numbers where exactly $ n $ digits are $ 1 $ and the remaining $ n $ digits are $ 2 $. Let $ g(n) $ denote the number of $ n $-digit numbers using only digits $ 1 $, $ 2 $, $ 3 $, and $ 4 $, with an equal number of $ 1 $'s and $ 2 $'s. Prove that $ f(n) = g(n) $.

Let $M$ be the intersection point of diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ in a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$. If the angle bisector of $\angle ACD$ intersects the extension of $BA$ at a point $K$, and $MA \cdot MC + MA \cdot CD = MB \cdot MD$, prove that $\angle BKC = \angle CDB$.

Let $ p, q, r $ be positive real numbers. Prove the inequality $$\frac{1}{q + r} + \frac{1}{r + p} + \frac{1}{p + q} \geq \frac{9}{2(p + q + r)}.$$ Using this, show that for any real number $ m > 1 $, the inequality $$\frac{p^m}{q + r} + \frac{q^m}{r + p} + \frac{r^m}{p + q} \geq \frac{(p + q + r)^{m - 1}}{2 \cdot 3^{m - 2}}$$ holds.
Determine all integer pairs $(x, y)$ that satisfy the equation $7(x + y) = 3(x^2 - xy + y^2)$.

Given triangle $\triangle ABC$ with side lengths $AB = c$, $BC = a$, and $CA = b$, and circumradius $R$, consider two circles $K_1$ and $K_2$ that pass through point $C$ and are tangent to segment $AB$ at points $A$ and $B$, respectively. Let $K$ be a circle of radius $r$ that is externally tangent to both $K_1$ and $K_2$ and tangent to line $AB$.

a. Express $r$ in terms of $a, b, c$ and $R$.

b. If $r = \frac{R}{4}$, determine the measure of angle $\angle C$.

Let $D$ be a point on the side $BC$ of triangle $ABC$ such that $AB + BD = AC + CD$. Let the incircle of triangle $ABC$ intersect the segment $AD$ at two points $X$ and $Y$, with $X$ closer to $A$. Let $E$ be the point where the incircle touches side $BC$. Prove that:
(i) $EY$ is perpendicular to $AD$,
(ii) $XD = 2IA'$, where $I$ is the incentre of triangle $ABC$ and $A'$ is the midpoint of side $BC$.
Suppose $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral satisfying $AD + BC = AB$. Prove that the intersection point of the internal angle bisectors of $\angle ADC$ and $\angle BCD$ lies on the line $AB$.

Let $A$, $B$, and $C$ be real numbers satisfying the following conditions:
(i) $\sin A \cos B + |\cos A \sin B| = \sin A |\cos A| + |\sin B \cos B|$,
(ii) $\tan C$ and $\cot C$ are defined.
Determine the minimum value of $(\tan C - \sin A)^2 + (\cot C - \cos B)^2$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with side lengths $BC = a$, $CA = b$, and $AB = c$. Prove that
$$
\frac{\cos A}{a^3} + \frac{\cos B}{b^3} + \frac{\cos C}{c^3} \ge \frac{3}{2abc}.
$$

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$, and let $O$ be the centre of its incircle. Suppose the incircle touches $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ at points $K$, $L$, and $M$ respectively. Let $N$ be the intersection point of $OL$ and $KM$, and define $Q$ as the intersection of $BN$ with $CA$. Let $P$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BQ$. If it is given that $BP = AP + 2PQ$, find all possible values of $\frac{AB}{BC}$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle C = 90^\circ$. The altitude from $C$ to $AB$ meets $AB$ at point $D$. Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of triangle $BCD$. A circle $\omega_1$ lies inside triangle $ACD$ and is tangent to $AD$ and $AC$ at points $M$ and $N$, respectively, and is also tangent to $\omega$.
(i) Prove the identity $BD \cdot CN + BC \cdot DM = CD \cdot BM$.
(ii) Prove that $BM = BC$.

Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be positive real numbers satisfying $abc = 1$. Prove the inequality
$$
\sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{1}{a^2(b + c)} \ge \frac{3}{2}.
$$

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle BAC = 2\angle ACB$. Let $O$ be the center of the excircle opposite $A$, which is tangent to $BC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AC$, and let $P$ be the point where line $MO$ intersects $BC$. Prove that $AB = BP$.

Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$, where $AB > AC$. Suppose a line passing through $I$ is perpendicular to $AI$ and intersects the extension of $BC$ at a point $P$. Prove that $IP^2 = BP \cdot CP$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $M$ as the midpoint of side $BC$. Consider a circle passing through $A$ and tangent to $BC$ at $M$. This circle intersects $AB$ and $AC$ again at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. If the points $B$, $C$, $E$, and $D$ lie on a circle, prove that $AB = AC$.

Let the sequence $\{a_n\}$ satisfy $a_1 = 4$ and $a_{n+1} \ge a_n + n + 2$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Prove that the inequality
$$
\sum_{k=1}^{2010} \frac{1}{a_k} < \frac{3}{2}
$$
holds.

Let $a, b, c, d$ be positive real numbers with $a, b, c, d \ge 1$. Prove the following inequalities: 

a. $ abcd(a + b + c + d - 4)^4 \ge (a - 1)(b - 1)(c - 1)(d - 1)(a + b + c + d)^4 $, 

b. $ \dfrac{d}{a + b + c} + \dfrac{a}{b + c + d} + \dfrac{b}{c + d + a} + \dfrac{c}{d + a + b} \ge \dfrac{4}{3} $.
Determine a function $f : [0, \infty) \to [0, \infty)$ such that $f(2x + 1) = 4f(x) + 9$ holds for all $x \in [0, \infty)$.
Suppose $ f: \mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\} \to \mathbb{R} $ satisfies the identity $$ \frac{2}{x}f(-x) + f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) = x $$ for all $ x \ne 0 $. Determine $ f(8) $.

Suppose $a$, $b$, and $c$ are distinct nonzero real numbers such that the cubic equations $ax^3 + bx + c = 0$, $bx^3 + cx + a = 0$, and $cx^3 + ax + b = 0$ share a common root. Prove that at least one of these equations has three real roots (not necessarily distinct).
Determine all integer pairs $ (a, b) $ such that $ (b^2 + 11(a - b))^2 = a^3 b $.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. A point $P$ lies inside $\triangle ABC$ such that $\angle BCP = 30^\circ$, $\angle APB = 150^\circ$, and $\angle CAP = 39^\circ$. Determine the measure of $\angle BAP$.

Let \triangle ABC be a triangle with area 1 and AB > AC. The internal angle bisector of \angle A intersects BC at D. Let C' be the reflection of C across AD, and suppose that \triangle DBC' is similar to \triangle ABC. Determine the length of AB when the perimeter of \triangle ABC is minimised.

Let $ k $ be a real number satisfying $ -1 < k < 1 $. Suppose the line $ y = x + k $ intersects the parabola $ y = 1 - x^2 $ at points $ A $ and $ B $. Let $ C = (1, 0) $. Determine the maximum possible area of triangle $ ABC $.

Given triangle $ABC$ such that $\angle ABC > \angle BCA$ and $\angle BCA \ge 30^\circ$, let the angle bisectors of $\angle ABC$ and $\angle BCA$ intersect $AC$ and $AB$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. Let $BD$ and $CE$ intersect at point $P$ with $PD = PE$. If the inradius of triangle $ABC$ is 1, find the maximum possible value of the length $BC$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let $D$ and $E$ lie on $AB$ and $AC$ respectively such that $DE \parallel BC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. A point $P$ is given with $DB = DP$, $EC = EP$, and the open segment $AP$ intersects $BC$. If $\angle BPD = \angle CME$, prove that $\angle CPE = \angle BMD$.
Given triangle $ABC$ with $\angle BAC = 54^\circ$ and $\angle ACB = 24^\circ$, let $P$ be a point on segment $AC$ such that $AP = BC$. Determine the measure of $\angle CBP$.

Given an integer $n \ge 2$, consider $n$ distinct circles in the plane such that any two intersect at two distinct points and no three circles share a common intersection. Place a coin at each intersection point. Players $X$ and $Y$ take turns removing a coin, starting with $X$, with the rule that a player cannot remove a coin lying on the same circle as the last coin removed by the other player. The player who cannot make a move loses. Determine for which values of $n$ player $Y$ has a winning strategy.

Let $ ABC $ be a triangle with integer side lengths and perimeter $ 65 $. Let $ M $ be the midpoint of $ BC $, and let the incircle of $ \triangle ABC $ touch sides $ AB $ and $ AC $ at points $ E $ and $ F $, respectively. Let $ D $ be the projection of $ M $ onto $ EF $. If the quadrilateral $ ADMI $ is a parallelogram, where $ I $ is the incenter of $ \triangle ABC $, determine the product $ AB \times BC \times CA $.

\text{Given a trapezium } ABCD \text{ such that } AB \parallel CD, \text{ let } M \text{ and } N \text{ denote the midpoints of } AB \text{ and } CD, \text{ respectively. If the lengths of the diagonals } AC = 6, BD = 8, \text{ and the length of the segment } MN = 4, \text{ determine the area of trapezium } ABCD.
Determine the sum of all integer values of $k$ such that the quadratic equation $kx^2 + (4k - 2)x + (4k - 7) = 0$ has at least one integer root.

Let a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ be inscribed in a circle with center $O$. Denote by $E$ the intersection of diagonals $AC$ and $BD$. Let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of the arcs $AB$ and $CD$, respectively, that do not contain any other vertices. Let $P$ be the point where the line $EO$ intersects the segment $MN$. Given $BC = 5$, $AC = 11$, $BD = 12$, and $AD = 10$, determine the ratio $\frac{MN}{NP}$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with internal angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ meeting $BC$ at $D$. Consider a circle $\Gamma$ passing through $A$ and tangent to $BC$ at $D$. Let $\Gamma$ intersect $AB$ and $AC$ again at $E$ and $F$, respectively. Let lines $BF$ and $CE$ intersect $\Gamma$ again at $P$ and $Q$. Suppose lines $AP$ and $AQ$ intersect $BC$ at points $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Prove that the segment $XY$ is half the length of $BC$.
Let $\{a_n\}$ be the sequence defined recursively by $a_1 = 5$ and $a_{n+1} = a_n^2 - 3a_n + 3$ for all $n \geq 1$. Prove that $a_n > 3^{2^{n-1}}$ for all positive integers $n$.

Let $\{a_n\}$ be a sequence of integers such that for every positive integer $n$, the recurrence relation $a_n + a_{n+1} = 2a_{n+2}a_{n+3} + 2016$ holds. Determine all possible values of the initial terms $a_1$ and $a_2$.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. A circle $\Gamma$, externally tangent to $AC$ at point $C$, contains a point $D$ such that the circumcircle of triangle $ABD$ is internally tangent to $\Gamma$. If the segment $AD$ intersects $\Gamma$ again at a point $E$, prove that the line $BE$ is tangent to $\Gamma$.
Determine the value of the real number $a$ such that the function $f(x) = \frac{a}{x-1} + \frac{1}{x-2} + \frac{1}{x-6}$, defined on the open interval $(3, 5)$, achieves its maximum at $x = 4$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. Let $\Gamma$ denote the incircle of $\triangle ABC$ with centre $I$, which touches $AB$ and $AC$ at points $F$ and $E$, respectively. Let $\Omega$ be the circumcircle of triangle $AFE$. The two external common tangents of $\Gamma$ and $\Omega$ intersect at a point $P$. Suppose one of these external common tangents is parallel to $AC$. Prove that $\angle PBI = 90^\circ$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral inscribed in a circle $\Gamma$ with $AB = AD$. Choose a point $E$ on segment $CD$ such that $DE = BC$. The line $AE$ intersects $\Gamma$ again at $F$. Let $M$ be the intersection of chords $AC$ and $BF$, and let $P$ be the reflection of $C$ over $M$. Prove that the lines $PE$ and $BF$ are parallel.
Determine all real numbers $a$, $b$, and $c$ such that $$(2^{2a} + 1)(2^{2b} + 2)(2^{2c} + 8) = 2^{a + b + c + 5}.$$

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle such that $AC = kAB$ for some $k > 1$. The angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects $BC$ at $D$. A circle with $AC$ as its diameter intersects the extension of $AD$ at point $E$. Determine the ratio $\frac{AD}{AE}$ as a function of $k$.

In an acute triangle $ABC$ with $BC > AB$, let point $D$ lie on segment $AC$ such that $BD = BA$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Let $E$ be the intersection of the tangents at $D$ and $M$ to the circumcircle of triangle $CDM$. If line $BE$ intersects side $AC$ at point $F$, show that points $A$, $B$, $M$, and $F$ lie on a circle.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle inscribed in a circle $\Gamma$, and let $P$ be the midpoint of the arc $BC$ not containing $A$. Suppose $AP$ intersects $BC$ at $D$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of segment $AB$. Let $E$ be the point such that $AE$ is perpendicular to $AB$ and $BE$ is perpendicular to $MP$. Prove that $AE = DE$.

Let $n$ be an even integer with $n \ge 4$, and consider an $n \times n$ chessboard where adjacent cells are alternately coloured black and white. Let $A$ and $B$ be two interior cells (not on the boundary) of opposite colours. Show that there exists a Hamiltonian path from $A$ to $B$ on the chessboard, where the path moves between adjacent cells.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with centroid $G$ and midpoint $M$ of side $BC$. Let $D$ be a point on segment $GM$, and let a line through $D$ intersect sides $AB$ and $AC$ at points $E$ and $F$ respectively (with $E, F \ne A$). Prove that $$ [BEGF] + [CFGE] \ge \frac{4}{9}[ABC]. $$ Determine the condition under which equality holds.

Let $n$ be an integer and consider a set $A$ of $4n+2$ elements chosen from $\{0, 1, 2, 3, \dots, 5^n\}$. Show that there are three elements $a, b, c \in A$ with $a < b < c$ and satisfying $c + 2a > 3b$.

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with acute angle $\angle B$. A circle is tangent to sides $BC$, $CD$, and $DA$. This circle intersects the diagonal $AC$ at two points $M$ and $N$, with $M$ closer to $A$. If $AM = 9$, $MN = 16$, and $NC = 2$, determine the area of $ABCD$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be such that $AB < AC$. Suppose the internal angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects side $BC$ at point $D$, and the external angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects the extension of side $BC$ at point $E$. Given that $EB = 2022$ and both $BD$ and $DC$ are integers, determine the number of possible integer values for $BD$.

Let $a$ and $b$ be the solutions to the equation $x^{\frac{4}{3}} - 2022x^{\frac{2}{3}} + 2023 = 0$. Define $p = a + 3a^{\frac{1}{3}}b^{\frac{2}{3}}$ and $q = b + 3a^{\frac{2}{3}}b^{\frac{1}{3}}$. Determine the value of $(p+q)^{\frac{1}{3}} + (p-q)^{\frac{1}{3}}$.

Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients, and consider the sequence $\{a_n\}$ defined recursively by $a_0 = 0$ and $a_n = P(a_{n-1})$ for all $n \ge 1$. Suppose there exists a positive integer $m$ such that $a_m = 0$. Prove that at least one of $a_1$ or $a_2$ is zero.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral, with diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersecting at point $E$. Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on segment $AC$ in the order $A$, $E$, $Q$, $P$, $C$. It is given that $BP$ is the angle bisector of $\angle ABC$ and $DQ$ is the angle bisector of $\angle ADC$. If $AE = 4$, $EQ = 2$, and $QP = 3$, determine the value of $PC$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with circumcenter $O$. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $E$. Points $F$ and $G$ lie on segments $AB$ and $CD$ respectively, with $AF = 15$, $FB = 13$, $BE = 30$, $ED = 13$, $DG = 7.5$, and $GC = 6.5$. Let $P$ be a point such that $PF \perp AB$ and $PG \perp CD$. Determine the value of $\frac{PE}{PO}$.
Let $S$ be a set of $n$ binary sequences of length 200 such that the Hamming distance between any two distinct sequences in $S$ is at least 101. Is it possible for $n$ to be at least 101?

Given a convex polygon $P = A_1A_2\dots A_n$ with $n \ge 4$, define $f(i)$ to be the maximum angle $\angle A_iA_jA_{i+1}$ among all choices of $A_j$ that are distinct from $A_i$ and $A_{i+1}$ (with the convention $A_{n+1} = A_1$). Determine the minimum possible value of the sum $f(1) + f(2) + \dots + f(n)$ over all such polygons and for each $n$.

Let $ M $ be the midpoint of side $ BC $ in an acute triangle $ \triangle ABC $, and let $ D $ be the foot of the perpendicular from $ C $ to $ AM $. If the circumcircle of triangle $ ABD $ intersects $ BC $ again at a point $ E $ different from $ B $, and a point $ F $ lies on segment $ AE $ such that $ FB = FC $, prove that $ F $ is the midpoint of $ AE $.

Given a trapezium $ABCD$ with $AD \parallel BC$, $AD > BC$, and $AB = CD$, there exists a point $P$ such that the distances from $P$ to the vertices are $PA = 1$, $PB = 2$, $PC = 3$, and $PD = 4$. Compute the ratio $AD : BC$.

Let $ABCD$ be a square. A point $P$ lies inside the square such that $\angle APD + \angle BPC = 180^\circ$ and $\angle BPC < 90^\circ$. Given that $PB = 3$ and $PC = 4$, determine the length of side $BC$.

In triangle $ABC$, it is given that $\angle BAC = 75^\circ$ and $\angle ACB = 45^\circ$. The segment $BC$ is extended to a point $T$ such that $BC = CT$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AT$. Determine the measure of $\angle BMC$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB > AC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Let $I$ be the incenter of $\triangle ABC$, and let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $I$ onto $BC$. Suppose a line through $A$ is drawn perpendicular to $BC$, and this line intersects the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ again at a point $E \neq A$. If $\angle MID = \angle ACB - \angle ABC$, prove that $DE = DI$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $AB < AC$. The angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ meets $BC$ at point $D$. A circle $\Gamma$ passes through $A$ and $D$ and is tangent to $BC$ at $D$. This circle intersects $AB$ again at a point $E \neq A$. The tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $BDE$ at $D$ intersects $\Gamma$ again at a point $F \neq D$. Let $P$ be the intersection of $EF$ and $AC$. Prove that $PD$ is perpendicular to $BC$.
Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle, and let $P$ be a point inside it with $AP = 15$ and $BP = 8$. Determine the maximum possible value of the sum of the areas of triangles $ABP$ and $BCP$.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral such that $AB = 5$, $AD = 17$, and $CD = 6$. Suppose that the angle bisectors of $\angle BAD$ and $\angle ADC$ intersect at the midpoint of side $BC$. Determine the area of quadrilateral $ABCD$.
Determine the number of solutions to the equation $\log_3 x = 3 \sin(3\pi x)$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with incenter $I$. Suppose a point $P$ lies inside the triangle and satisfies the condition
$$
\angle PBA + \angle PCA = \angle PBC + \angle PCB.
$$
Prove that $AP \geq AI$, with equality if and only if $P = I$.

Let $ABCD$ be a trapezoid with $AB$ and $CD$ as parallel sides, where $AB > CD$. Points $K$ and $L$ are located on segments $AB$ and $CD$, respectively, such that the ratio $\frac{AK}{KB}$ equals $\frac{DL}{LC}$. Suppose that points $P$ and $Q$ exist on segment $KL$ satisfying the conditions
$$
\angle APB = \angle BCD \quad \text{and} \quad \angle CQD = \angle ABC.
$$
Show that the points $P$, $Q$, $B$, and $C$ lie on a single circle.

In triangle $ABC$, where $\angle C < \angle A < 90^\circ$, a point $D$ is selected on side $AC$ such that $BD = BA$. Let the incircle of triangle $ABC$ touch sides $AB$ and $AC$ at points $K$ and $L$, respectively, and let $J$ denote the incenter of triangle $BCD$. Prove that the line $KL$ intersects segment $AJ$ at its midpoint.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral and let $P$ be a point inside $ABCD$ such that the circles passing through $A$ and $D$, and $B$ and $C$, are externally tangent at $P$. If $$\angle PAB + \angle PDC \leq 90^\circ \quad \text{ and } \quad \angle PBA + \angle PCD \leq 90^\circ,$$ prove that the inequality $AB + CD \geq BC + AD$ holds.

Let $a > b > 1$ be relatively prime positive integers. For an integer $c$, define its weight $w(c)$ as the minimum value of $|x| + |y|$ over all integer solutions $(x, y)$ of the equation $$ a x + b y = c. $$ A number $c$ is termed a local champion if $w(c) \geq w(c + a)$, $w(c) \geq w(c - a)$, $w(c) \geq w(c + b)$, and $w(c) \geq w(c - b)$. Determine all local champions and count how many such integers exist.

Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ be a sequence of real numbers. For each $1 \leq i \leq n$, define $d_i = \max\{a_j : 1 \leq j \leq i\} - \min\{a_j : i \leq j \leq n\}$, and let $d = \max\{d_i : 1 \leq i \leq n\}$.

(a) Prove that for any non-decreasing sequence $x_1 \leq x_2 \leq \cdots \leq x_n$ of real numbers, it holds that $$\max\{ |x_i - a_i| : 1 \leq i \leq n \} \geq \frac{d}{2}.$$

(b) Show that there exists a non-decreasing sequence $x_1 \leq x_2 \leq \cdots \leq x_n$ for which equality is achieved in the inequality above.
Determine all possible values of $f(2007)$ for functions $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for all positive integers $m$ and $n$, the inequality $f(m+n) \geq f(m) + f(f(n)) - 1$ holds.

Consider a unit square partitioned into $n > 1$ rectangles with their sides parallel to those of the square. Suppose that for any line parallel to a side of the square that intersects the square’s interior, it also intersects the interior of at least one rectangle. Prove that at least one rectangle in the partition has no point lying on the boundary of the square.

Let $A_0 = (a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n)$ be a sequence of real numbers. For each $k \geq 0$, define a new sequence $A_{k+1}$ from $A_k = (x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)$ as follows:
1. Choose a partition of $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ into two disjoint subsets $I$ and $J$ such that the absolute difference $\left|\sum_{i \in I} x_i - \sum_{j \in J} x_j\right|$ is minimized. If multiple such partitions exist, choose one arbitrarily.
2. Define $A_{k+1} = (y_1, y_2, \dots, y_n)$, where $y_i = x_i + 1$ if $i \in I$, and $y_i = x_i - 1$ if $i \in J$.
Prove that there exists some $k$ such that the sequence $A_k$ contains an element $x$ with $|x| \geq n / 2$.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Consider a point $X$ moving along the shorter arc $MA$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABM$. Define a point $T$ in the interior of angle $BMA$ such that $\angle TMX = 90^\circ$ and $TX = BX$. Show that the difference $\angle MTB - \angle CTM$ is constant, independent of the position of $X$.

Find the minimal positive real number $ k $ such that for any convex quadrilateral $ ABCD $, and points $ A_1, B_1, C_1, D_1 $ on sides $ AB, BC, CD, DA $ respectively, if $ S $ denotes the sum of the two smallest areas among the triangles $ AA_1D_1, BB_1A_1, CC_1B_1, DD_1C_1 $, and $ S_1 $ is the area of quadrilateral $ A_1B_1C_1D_1 $, then the inequality $ k S_1 \geq S $ always holds.

Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ be positive real numbers satisfying $abcd = 1$ and $a + b + c + d > \frac{a}{b} + \frac{b}{c} + \frac{c}{d} + \frac{d}{a}$. Prove that $a + b + c + d < \frac{b}{a} + \frac{c}{b} + \frac{d}{c} + \frac{a}{d}$.

Let $a, b, c, d$ be positive real numbers. Prove that $$\frac{(a-b)(a-c)}{a+b+c} + \frac{(b-c)(b-d)}{b+c+d} + \frac{(c-d)(c-a)}{c+d+a} + \frac{(d-a)(d-b)}{d+a+b} \geq 0,$$ and determine when equality occurs.
Determine all functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all real numbers $x$ and $y$, the following equation holds: $$ f\left(x f(x+y)\right) = f\left(y f(x)\right) + x^2. $$

Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let the incircle touch sides $AB$ and $AC$ at points $Z$ and $Y$, respectively. Suppose $G$ is the intersection point of lines $BY$ and $CZ$. Let $R$ and $S$ be defined such that $BCYR$ and $BCSZ$ are parallelograms. Prove that $GR = GS$.
Let $P$ be a convex polygon symmetric about a point $O$. Show that there exists a parallelogram $R$ with $P \subset R$ such that $$\frac{\text{Area}(R)}{\text{Area}(P)} \leq \sqrt{2}.$$

Consider a round-robin tournament with $ n \geq 4 $ players where each pair of players plays exactly one game and there are no draws. A set of four players is defined as bad if one player loses to the other three, and among those three, each has one win and one loss against the others. Assume there are no bad sets in the tournament. Let $ w_i $ and $ \ell_i $ denote the number of wins and losses of player $ i $, respectively. Prove that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} \left( w_i - \ell_i \right)^3 \geq 0.
$$

Let $P_1, P_2, \dots, P_s$ be arithmetic progressions of integers such that:
(1) every integer is included in at least one of the progressions;
(2) each progression contains an element not included in any other progression.
Let $n$ be the least common multiple of the common differences of these progressions, with prime factorization $n = p_1^{\alpha_1} p_2^{\alpha_2} \cdots p_k^{\alpha_k}$. Prove the inequality
$$
s \geq 1 + \sum_{i=1}^{k} \alpha_i(p_i - 1).
$$

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$, and let $D$ be the midpoint of side $AC$. The bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects the circumcircle of triangle $DBC$ at a point $E$ inside triangle $ABC$. The line $BD$ intersects the circumcircle of triangle $AEB$ again at a point $F$. Let $I$ be the intersection of lines $AF$ and $BE$, and let $K$ be the intersection of lines $CI$ and $BD$. Prove that $I$ is the incenter of triangle $KAB$.

Let $ABCDEF$ be a convex hexagon such that all its sides are tangent to a circle $\omega$ centered at $O$. Assume that the circumcircle of triangle $ACE$ is concentric with $\omega$. Let $J$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $B$ to $CD$. If the perpendicular from $B$ to $DF$ meets the line $EO$ at a point $K$, and $L$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $K$ to $DE$, prove that $DJ = DL$.

Let triangle $ABC$ have a right angle at $C$, and let $C_0$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $C$ to $AB$. Select a point $X$ strictly between $C$ and $C_0$ on segment $CC_0$. Define points $K$ and $L$ on $AX$ and $BX$ respectively such that $BK = BC$ and $AL = AC$. Let $M$ be the point where $AL$ and $BK$ intersect. Prove that $MK = ML$.

Show that for any set $S$ of $2000$ distinct real numbers, there are distinct pairs $(a, b)$ and $(c, d)$ in $S$ with $a > b$ and $c > d$, such that $$ \left|\frac{a - b}{c - d} - 1\right| < \frac{1}{100000}. $$

Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $A$ be a subset of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$. An $A$-partition of $n$ into $k$ parts is a representation $n = a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_k$, where each $a_i$ is an element of $A$, and repetitions are allowed. The number of different parts in such a partition is defined as the cardinality of the set $\{a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k\}$. An $A$-partition is called optimal if it uses the minimum number of parts among all $A$-partitions of $n$. Prove that any optimal $A$-partition of $n$ contains at most $\sqrt[3]{6n}$ distinct elements.

Let $n \geqslant 2$ be an integer. A circular arrangement of the numbers $0, 1, \ldots, n$ is considered up to rotation, so there are $n+1$ rotations of any arrangement that are considered equivalent. A circular arrangement is called beautiful if for any four distinct numbers $a, b, c, d$ in $\{0, 1, \ldots, n\}$ such that $a + c = b + d$, the chord connecting $a$ and $c$ does not intersect the chord connecting $b$ and $d$. Let $M$ be the number of such beautiful arrangements, and let $N$ be the number of pairs $(x, y)$ of positive integers with $x + y \leqslant n$ and $\gcd(x, y) = 1$. Prove that $M = N + 1$.

Let triangle $ABC$ satisfy $\angle B > \angle C$. Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on line $AC$ such that $\angle PBA = \angle QBA = \angle ACB$, with $A$ between $P$ and $C$. Let $D$ be an interior point on segment $BQ$ such that $PD = PB$. The ray $AD$ intersects the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ again at point $R$. Prove that $QB = QR$.

Let $A B C D E F$ be a convex hexagon such that $AB = DE$, $BC = EF$, and $CD = FA$, and the angle differences satisfy $\angle A - \angle D = \angle C - \angle F = \angle E - \angle B$. Prove that the diagonals $AD$, $BE$, and $CF$ are concurrent.

Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer, and consider an $n \times n$ chessboard. A configuration of $n$ rooks is called happy if each row and each column contains exactly one rook. Determine the largest integer $k$ such that, in any happy configuration, there exists an empty $k \times k$ subgrid (i.e., a square of size $k \times k$ containing no rooks).

Given $n \geq 3$ lines in the plane with no two parallel and no three concurrent, let $\mathcal{F}$ denote the set of all bounded regions formed by these lines. Prove that it is possible to colour $\left\lceil\sqrt{n/2}\right\rceil$ lines blue such that no region in $\mathcal{F}$ is bounded entirely by blue lines.

Let $M$ be a set of $n \geq 4$ points in the plane, with no three collinear. Initially, the points are connected by $n$ segments such that each point has degree 2 in the resulting graph. At each step, if two segments $AB$ and $CD$ intersect at a point in their interiors, and the segments $AC$ and $BD$ are not yet present, they may be replaced by $AC$ and $BD$. Prove that it is impossible to perform $\frac{n^3}{4}$ or more such replacement operations.

In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$, points $P$ and $Q$ are selected on side $BC$ such that $\angle PAB = \angle ACB$ and $\angle QAC = \angle CBA$. Let $M$ and $N$ be points on the rays $AP$ and $AQ$ respectively, such that $AP = PM$ and $AQ = QN$. Prove that the lines $BM$ and $CN$ meet at a point lying on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.

Let $\Omega$ and $O$ be the circumcircle and the circumcenter of an acute triangle $ABC$ with $AB > BC$. The internal angle bisector of $\angle ABC$ intersects $\Omega$ again at a point $M$. Let $\Gamma$ be the circle with diameter $BM$. The angle bisectors of $\angle AOB$ and $\angle BOC$ intersect $\Gamma$ again at points $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Choose a point $R$ on line $PQ$ such that $BR = MR$. Prove that $BR \parallel AC$.

There are $n \geqslant 1$ towns arranged in a line from left to right in Lineland. Each town has a left bulldozer (on the left side of the town, facing left) and a right bulldozer (on the right side of the town, facing right). All $2n$ bulldozers have distinct sizes. When a right bulldozer and a left bulldozer meet, the larger one pushes the smaller one off the road. Additionally, if a bulldozer reaches the rear of another bulldozer, it pushes it off the road regardless of size. For two towns $A$ and $B$, where $B$ lies to the right of $A$, we say $A$ can sweep $B$ away if the right bulldozer of $A$ can reach $B$ and eliminate all bulldozers along the way. Similarly, $B$ can sweep $A$ away if the left bulldozer of $B$ can reach $A$ and eliminate all bulldozers in its path. Prove that there is exactly one town that cannot be swept away by any other town.

Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane. The set $\mathcal{S}$ is called balanced if, for any pair of distinct points $A, B \in \mathcal{S}$, there exists a point $C \in \mathcal{S}$ such that $AC = BC$. The set $\mathcal{S}$ is called center-free if, for any distinct points $A, B, C \in \mathcal{S}$, there is no point $P \in \mathcal{S}$ such that $PA = PB = PC$.

(a) Prove that for every integer $n \geq 3$, there exists a balanced set with exactly $n$ points.

(b) Determine all integers $n \geq 3$ for which there exists a balanced and center-free set with exactly $n$ points.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB > AC$, and let $\Gamma$ denote its circumcircle. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$, $M$ the midpoint of side $BC$, and $F$ the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$. Let $Q$ and $K$ be points on $\Gamma$ such that $\angle AQH = 90^\circ$ and $\angle QKH = 90^\circ$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $KQH$ and $KFM$ are tangent to each other.

Determine all integers $n \geqslant 3$ such that for any real numbers $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ and $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$ with $\left|a_{k}\right| + \left|b_{k}\right| = 1$ for each $1 \leqslant k \leqslant n$, there exists a sequence $x = (x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n})$ with $x_{k} \in \{-1, 1\}$ for all $k$, satisfying
$$
\left|\sum_{k=1}^{n} x_{k} a_{k}\right| + \left|\sum_{k=1}^{n} x_{k} b_{k}\right| \leqslant 1.
$$

Let $ n \geq 2 $ be an integer. The plane contains $ n $ segments such that every pair of segments intersects at a unique interior point, and no three segments share a common intersection point. Jeff places a snail at one endpoint of each segment and claps his hands $ n-1 $ times. With each clap, all snails move to the next intersection point along their segments and remain there until the next clap. Since each segment contains exactly $ n-1 $ interior intersection points, after $ n-1 $ claps, all snails reach the farthest intersection point from their starting endpoint.\text{a) Prove that if $ n $ is odd, Jeff can always assign snail starting points so that no two snails ever share the same intersection point at any time.\text{b) Prove that if $ n $ is even, then regardless of how Jeff assigns the snail starting points, there will always be a time when at least two snails occupy the same intersection point.}

Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function such that for all real numbers $x$ and $y$ with $(f(x)+y)(f(y)+x) > 0$, it holds that $f(x)+y = f(y)+x$. Show that for all $x > y$, we have $f(x)+y \leq f(y)+x$.

Let $n \geq 3$ be an integer. Suppose two regular $n$-gons $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ are placed in the plane. Show that any vertex of $\mathcal{A}$ contained in the interior or boundary of $\mathcal{B}$ must form a consecutive sequence among the vertices of $\mathcal{A}$. In particular, there exists a straight line that separates the vertices of $\mathcal{A}$ inside $\mathcal{B}$ from those outside $\mathcal{B}$.

Let $n \geq 2018$ be an integer, and let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ and $b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$ be pairwise distinct positive integers all less than or equal to $5n$. Assume that the sequence $\frac{a_1}{b_1}, \frac{a_2}{b_2}, \ldots, \frac{a_n}{b_n}$ forms an arithmetic progression. Prove that all terms in the sequence are equal.
Find all integer-valued functions $f: \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ satisfying the functional equation $f(2a) + 2f(b) = f(f(a + b))$ for every pair of integers $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$.

Let $ x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{2019} $ be real numbers such that $ \sum_{i=1}^{2019} x_i = 0 $ and $ \sum_{i=1}^{2019} x_i^2 = 1 $. Define $ m = \min\{x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{2019}\} $ and $ M = \max\{x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{2019}\} $. Prove that $ mM \leq -\frac{1}{2019} $.

Let $ n \geq 2 $ be an integer and $ a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n $ be real numbers with $ a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_n = 0 $. Define $ A = \{ (i, j) \mid 1 \leq i < j \leq n, \, |a_i - a_j| \geq 1 \} $. Show that if $ A \neq \emptyset $, then $ \sum_{(i,j) \in A} a_i a_j < 0 $.

Let $P(x, y, z)$ be a polynomial in three variables with real coefficients such that
$$
P(x, y, z) = P(x, y, xy - z) = P(x, xz - y, z) = P(yz - x, y, z)
$$
Show that there exists a polynomial $F(t)$ in one variable for which
$$
P(x, y, z) = F\left(x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz\right)
$$

Let $n$ be a positive integer, and consider a sequence $C$ of $n$ coins, each of which is either heads ($H$) or tails ($T$). Define a process where if there are exactly $k$ heads in the sequence and $k > 0$, the $k^{	ext{th}}$ coin is flipped. This process continues until all coins are tails. Let $\ell(C)$ denote the number of steps required to reach this state. Prove that $\ell(C)$ is finite for any $C$, and compute the average of $\ell(C)$ over all $2^n$ possible configurations $C$.

Let $ G $ be a complete directed graph on $ n \geqslant 2 $ vertices, where the direction of each edge is initially unknown. An oracle can be queried to determine the direction of any given edge. The goal is to determine whether there exists at least one vertex in $ G $ with out-degree at most 1. Prove that it is always possible to achieve this goal with at most $ 4n $ queries to the oracle.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with altitudes $AD$, $BE$, and $CF$ intersecting sides $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ at $D$, $E$, and $F$, respectively. Let $\omega_{B}$ and $\omega_{C}$ be the incircles of triangles $BDF$ and $CDE$, tangent to $DF$ and $DE$ at points $M$ and $N$, respectively. Suppose that line $MN$ intersects $\omega_{B}$ and $\omega_{C}$ again at $P$ and $Q$ distinct from $M$ and $N$. Prove that $MP = NQ$.

Let $ABCDE$ be a convex pentagon with $CD = DE$ and $\angle EDC \neq 2 \cdot \angle ADB$. Suppose a point $P$ lies inside the pentagon such that $AP = AE$ and $BP = BC$. Prove that $P$ is on the diagonal $CE$ if and only if $\operatorname{area}(BCD) + \operatorname{area}(ADE) = \operatorname{area}(ABD) + \operatorname{area}(ABP)$.

Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the set of all lines in the Euclidean plane, and let $f: \mathcal{L} \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a function such that $f(\ell)$ lies on the line $\ell$ for every $\ell \in \mathcal{L}$. Suppose that for every point $X$ in the plane and any three distinct lines $\ell_1, \ell_2, \ell_3$ passing through $X$, the four points $f(\ell_1), f(\ell_2), f(\ell_3)$, and $X$ are concyclic. Prove that there exists a unique point $P$ such that for every line $\ell$ containing $P$, $f(\ell) = P$.

Given four positive real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, and $d$ satisfying $a \geq b \geq c \geq d > 0$ and $a + b + c + d = 1$, prove the inequality
$$
(a + 2b + 3c + 4d) \cdot a^a b^b c^c d^d < 1.
$$

Let $n$ be a positive integer. Consider an $n \times n$ matrix $A$ with entries $A_{i,j} = \left\lfloor\frac{ij}{n+1}\right\rfloor$ for all $i, j = 1, 2, \ldots, n$. Find all values of $n$ for which the sum of all entries of $A$ equals $\frac{1}{4} n^2(n - 1)$.

Let $n \geqslant 3$ be an integer. A positive integer $m$ with $m \geqslant n+1$ is defined to be $n$-colourful if, given an unlimited supply of marbles in $n$ distinct colours $C_{1}, C_{2}, \ldots, C_{n}$, one can arrange $m$ marbles in a circular pattern such that every sequence of $n+1$ consecutive marbles contains at least one marble of each colour $C_{i}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, n$. Show that only finitely many integers are not $n$-colourful and determine the maximum such integer.

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with $AC = BC$. Choose a point $P$ on the extension of $AB$ beyond $B$. Suppose the circumcircle of triangle $ACD$ intersects segment $PD$ again at point $Q$, and the circumcircle of triangle $APQ$ intersects segment $PC$ again at point $R$. Prove that the lines $CD$, $AQ$, and $BR$ are concurrent.
Find all integers $n \geq 3$ such that any convex polygon with $n$ sides, each of length $1$, must contain an equilateral triangle with side length $1$ as a subset of its boundary or interior.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle such that $AC > AB$, and let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$. Let $D$ be a point on segment $BC$. The line through $D$ perpendicular to $BC$ meets $AO$, $AC$, and $AB$ at points $W$, $X$, and $Y$, respectively. Let $Z$ be the second point of intersection of the circumcircles of triangles $AXY$ and $ABC$. Prove that if $OW = OD$, then the line $DZ$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $AXY$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let two parallel lines $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ intersect the sides $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ at points $X_i$, $Y_i$, and $Z_i$ for $i = 1,2$. For each $i$, consider the triangle $\Delta_i$ formed by the lines through $X_i$, $Y_i$, and $Z_i$ that are perpendicular to $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$, respectively. Assume that each $\Delta_i$ is non-degenerate. Prove that the circumcircles of $\Delta_1$ and $\Delta_2$ are tangent to each other.

Let $N$ be a positive integer. Show that it is possible to find three permutations $\alpha = (\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_N)$, $\beta = (\beta_1, \beta_2, \ldots, \beta_N)$, and $\gamma = (\gamma_1, \gamma_2, \ldots, \gamma_N)$ of the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, N\}$ such that for all $k = 1, 2, \ldots, N$, the inequality
$$
\left|\sqrt{\alpha_k} + \sqrt{\beta_k} + \sqrt{\gamma_k} - 2\sqrt{N}\right| < 2023
$$
holds.

Let $n$ be a positive integer, and consider a triangle of circles with $n$ rows, where the $i^\text{th}$ row contains exactly $i$ circles. A ninja-path is a sequence of circles starting at the top of the triangle and repeatedly moving to one of the two circles directly below. Suppose that exactly one circle is selected from each row and marked red. Determine the largest integer $k$ such that, regardless of how the red circles are chosen, there is always a ninja-path containing at least $k$ red circles.

Let triangle $ABC$ satisfy $AC > BC$, and let $\omega$ denote its circumcircle with radius $r$. Let $P$ be a point on segment $AC$ such that $BC = CP$, and let $S$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $P$ to line $AB$. If ray $BP$ intersects $\omega$ again at $D$, define a point $Q$ on line $SP$ such that $PQ = r$ and the points $S, P, Q$ appear in that order on the line. Let $E$ be the intersection of the line through $A$ perpendicular to $CQ$ and the line through $B$ perpendicular to $DQ$. Prove that $E$ lies on $\omega$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB < AC$, and let $\Omega$ be its circumcircle. Let $S$ be the midpoint of the arc $CAB$ of $\Omega$ not containing $B$. The altitude from $A$ to $BC$ intersects $BS$ at $D$ and $\Omega$ again at $E \neq A$. Let $L$ be the point where the line through $D$ parallel to $BC$ intersects $BE$. Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of triangle $BDL$, and let $P$ be the second intersection point of $\omega$ with $\Omega$. Prove that the tangent to $\omega$ at $P$ and the line $BS$ intersect on the internal angle bisector of $\angle BAC$.

Let $N$ be a positive integer. Geoff and Ceri play a game starting with the numbers $1, 2, \ldots, N$ written on a board. Geoff goes first, and players alternate turns. On each turn, a player selects a pair $(k, n)$ with $k \geqslant 0$ and $n$ an integer currently on the board, and removes all integers $s$ on the board such that $2^k$ divides $n - s$. The game ends when the board is empty, and the player who removes the last number loses. Determine all values of $N$ for which Geoff has a winning strategy, regardless of Ceri's actions.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with $AC < BD < AD$ and $\angle DBA < 90^\circ$. A point $E$ is chosen on the line through $D$ parallel to $AB$, on the opposite side of $AD$ from $C$, such that $AC = DE$. A point $F$ is chosen on the line through $A$ parallel to $CD$, on the opposite side of $AD$ from $C$, such that $BD = AF$. Prove that the perpendicular bisectors of $BC$ and $EF$ intersect at a point on the circumcircle of $ABCD$.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $AB \parallel CD$ and $AB < CD$. The lines $AD$ and $BC$ intersect at point $P$. Let $X$ be a point on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$, distinct from $C$, such that $PC = PX$. Similarly, let $Y$ be a point on the circumcircle of triangle $ABD$, distinct from $D$, such that $PD = PY$. If lines $AX$ and $BY$ intersect at $Q$, prove that $PQ$ is parallel to $AB$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB < AC$, and let $\Gamma$ denote its circumcircle. Let $X$ and $Y$ be points on $\Gamma$ such that the line $XY$ intersects $BC$ at a point lying on the external angle bisector of $\angle BAC$. Assume that the tangents to $\Gamma$ at $X$ and $Y$ meet at a point $T$ on the same side of $BC$ as $A$, and suppose that $TX$ and $TY$ intersect $BC$ at points $U$ and $V$, respectively. Let $J$ be the excenter of triangle $TUV$ opposite $T$. Prove that the segment $AJ$ bisects $\angle BAC$.
Determine all integer triples $(a, b, c)$ satisfying the system of equations: $a + b + c = 24$, $a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = 210$, and $abc = 440$.

Determine the positive real roots $r_1, r_2, r_3, r_4$ of the polynomial equation $4x^4 - a x^3 + b x^2 - c x + 5 = 0$, given the condition $\frac{r_1}{2} + \frac{r_2}{4} + \frac{r_3}{5} + \frac{r_4}{8} = 1$.

Let $x, y, z$ be real numbers with $x 
eq 1$, $y 
eq 1$, and $x 
eq y$. Given that $\dfrac{y z - x^2}{1 - x} = \dfrac{x z - y^2}{1 - y}$, prove that $\dfrac{y z - x^2}{1 - x} = x + y + z$.

Let $f : \mathbb{Z}^+ \to \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ be a function satisfying the following conditions:

1. $f(mn) = f(m) + f(n)$ for all positive integers $m, n$,
2. $f(n) = 0$ if the last digit of $n$ is $3$,
3. $f(10) = 0$.

Determine the value of $f(1985)$.
Determine a function $f(x)$ satisfying the identity $f(x)^2 f\left(\frac{1 - x}{1 + x}\right) = 64x$ for all $x \neq 0, \pm 1$.
Let $k$ be an odd positive integer, and suppose that $\displaystyle (2+\sqrt{3})^k = 1 + m + n \sqrt{3}$, where $m$ and $n$ are positive integers. Prove that $m$ is a perfect square.
Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, $p$, $q$ be positive integers such that $ad - bc = 1$ and $\frac{a}{b} > \frac{p}{q} > \frac{c}{d}$. Prove that $q \geq b + d$ and that $p = a + c$ when $q = b + d$.
Let $ P $ be a fixed point in the plane. Among all triangles $ ABC $ satisfying $ PA = 3 $, $ PB = 5 $, and $ PC = 7 $, prove that those with the maximum perimeter have $ P $ as their incenter.

Suppose $k$ satisfies $k^{3} = 2$, and let $x$, $y$, $z$ be rational numbers such that the expression $x + y k + z k^{2}$ is non-zero. Prove that there exist rational numbers $u$, $v$, and $w$ for which $(x + y k + z k^{2})(u + v k + w k^{2}) = 1$.
Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive real numbers such that $0 < x, y, z < \frac{\pi}{2}$. Prove the inequality $\frac{\pi}{2} + 2 \sin x \cos y + 2 \sin y \cos z > \sin 2x + \sin 2y + \sin 2z$.
Given that $ a $, $ b $, and $ c $ are the side lengths of a triangle, prove that $ \displaystyle \frac{a-b}{a+b} + \frac{b-c}{b+c} + \frac{c-a}{a+c} < \frac{1}{16} $.

Let $ f: \mathbb{Z}^+ \to \mathbb{Z}^+ $ be a function satisfying $ f(1) = 1 $, $ f(2n + 1) = f(2n) + 1 $, and $ f(2n) = 3f(n) $. Determine all values $ m $ such that there exists a positive integer $ n $ with $ f(n) = m $.
Prove that the Diophantine equation $2a^2 - 3a + 1 = 3b^2 + b$ has infinitely many solutions in positive integers $a$ and $b$.

Let $f: \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a function such that $f\left(2^{n} - 1\right) = 0$ for all $n \geq 0$. For all $m \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ not of the form $2^{n} - 1$, define $f(m) = f(m+1) + 1$. Prove that for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, there exists an integer $k$ such that $f(n) + n = 2^{k} - 1$, and determine the value of $f\left(2^{1990}\right)$.

Let $ f $ be a function defined on $ [0,1] $ satisfying $ f(0) = 0 $, $ f\left(\frac{x}{3}\right) = \frac{f(x)}{2} $, and $ f(1 - x) = 1 - f(x) $. Determine the value of $ f\left(\frac{18}{1991}\right) $.
Consider the function $f(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \dfrac{a_i}{x + a_i}$, where $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ are distinct positive real numbers. Determine the total length of the intervals where $f(x) \geq 1$.

Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle with side length $2$. Prove that for any point $P$ lying on the incircle of triangle $ABC$, it holds that $PA^{2} + PB^{2} + PC^{2} = 5$. Additionally, prove that the triangle formed with side lengths $PA$, $PB$, and $PC$ has area $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$.

Consider two integer sequences $a_n$ and $b_n$ defined by the initial conditions $a_0 = 0$, $b_0 = 8$, and the recurrence relations $a_{n+2} = 2a_{n+1} - a_n + 2$ and $b_{n+2} = 2b_{n+1} - b_n$. Suppose further that for all $n > 0$, the expression $a_n^2 + b_n^2$ is a perfect square. Determine at least two distinct pairs $(a_{1992}, b_{1992})$ satisfying these conditions.
Given a cyclic trapezoid $ABCD$ where $AB \parallel CD$, the distance between $AB$ and $CD$ is $h$, and the sum of the lengths of $AB$ and $CD$ is $m$, construct such a trapezoid.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle. On the ray $BA$, extend past $A$ to a point $A'$ such that $AA' = BC$, and on the ray $CA$, extend past $A$ to a point $A''$ such that $AA'' = BC$. Similarly, on the ray $CB$, extend past $B$ to a point $B'$ with $BB' = CA$, and on the ray $AB$, extend past $B$ to a point $B''$ with $BB'' = CA$. On the ray $AB$, extend past $C$ to a point $C'$ with $CC' = AB$, and on the ray $CB$, extend past $C$ to a point $C''$ with $CC'' = AB$. Prove that the area of the hexagon $A''A'B''B'C'C''$ is at least 13 times the area of triangle $ABC$.
Determine all strictly increasing functions $ f: \mathbb{Z}^+ \to \mathbb{Z}^+ $ such that $ f(y f(x)) = x^2 f(xy) $ for all positive integers $ x $ and $ y $.
Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle with points $D$ on $AB$ and $E$ on $AC$ such that the segment $DE$ is tangent to the incircle of $\triangle ABC$. Prove that $\frac{AD}{DB} + \frac{AE}{EC} = 1$.

Let $S$ be a finite set of $n > 1$ points in the plane, and for any two points $P, Q \in S$, let $m(PQ)$ denote the perpendicular bisector of the segment $PQ$. Suppose $S$ satisfies the following conditions:

(1) For any $P, Q \in S$, there is at least one point in $m(PQ)$ that also belongs to $S$,
